chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Muthanna, from his mother Fatima bint al-Husayn (peace be upon him). She said:

The crowd rushed into our pavilion while I was a young girl, and I had two gold anklets on my feet. A man began removing the two anklets from my feet while he was weeping. So I said: 'What makes you cry, O enemy of God?!' He said: 'How can I not weep when I am robbing the daughter of the Messenger of God!' So I said: 'Do not rob me.' He said: 'I fear someone else may come and take it.'
She said: And they plundered everything in the structures, to the point that they were pulling the cloaks off our backs.

key_terms.ابنة رسول الله: Daughter of the Messenger of God, emphasizing the sacred lineage of the victim
key_terms.الغاغة: The crowd or mob, referring to the Umayyad soldiers who looted the camp
key_terms.الفسطاط: Pavilion or tent, the encampment of Imam al-Husayn's family at Karbala
key_terms.خلخال: Anklet, a gold ornament worn on the feet

ai.seo_question: What happened to the family of Imam al-Husayn after the Battle of Karbala?
ai.summary: Fatima bint al-Husayn (AS), an eyewitness and survivor of the Battle of Karbala in 61 AH, recounts the looting that followed the massacre. Even the looters themselves wept at the horror of robbing the Prophet's family, yet feared that if they did not take the spoils, others would. This account illustrates the depth of injustice inflicted on the Ahl al-Bayt after the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (AS).
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Muhammad b Sinan from Abi’l Jarud Ziyad b. al-Mundhir from `Abdullah b. al-Hasan al-Muthanna from his mother Fatima bt. al-Husayn (as). She said:

The crowd came into our pavilion. I was a young girl, and I had gold anklets on my feet. A man rushed to take the anklets from my feet whilst he was weeping. So, I said: “What makes you cry, O enemy of Allah?!” So, he said: “How can I not weep when I am robbing the daughter of the Messenger of Allah?!” So, I said: “Do not rob me.” He said: “I fear someone else may take it.”
She said: They took everything in the buildings to the point where they even took the cloaks off our backs.
